faqs.question: What is the Reax top Vortex Mixer used for?
faqs.answer: The Reax top Vortex Mixer is a single-tube vortexer used to mix solutions, dissolve cell pellets, distribute solids, and homogenize viscous media. It mixes on the press of a tube in short-term mode, and runs hands-free in continuous mode for tougher dissolving work.

faqs.question: What is the maximum speed of the Reax top Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: The Reax top reaches up to 3,200 rpm, across two ranges: 100 to 2,500 rpm and 200 to 3,200 rpm. At full speed its 5 mm orbit homogenizes even highly viscous media.

faqs.question: What is the shaking orbit of the Reax top Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: The Reax top has a fixed 5 mm shaking orbit with a circular vibrating movement. Combined with speeds up to 3,200 rpm, this gives reliable, uniform distribution of solids and effective homogenization of viscous samples.

faqs.question: How does short-term mode work on the Reax top Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: In short-term mode, pressure on the tube tray triggers the shaking motion, and it runs while you hold the tube in place. It is designed for quickly mixing up solutions, one tube at a time.

faqs.question: Can the Reax top Vortex Mixer run continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes. Continuous operation keeps the Reax top running hands-free, which is how it dissolves persistent cell pellets gently but powerfully without you holding the tube.

faqs.question: Can the Reax top Vortex Mixer dissolve stubborn cell pellets?
faqs.answer: Yes. Continuous operation is designed for this: it works a persistent pellet gently but powerfully back into solution where a quick pulse would not shift it.

faqs.question: Can I repeat the same speed setting on the Reax top Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Speed is set on a scale with reference points, so once you find a setting that suits a given sample you can return to it.

faqs.question: How much does the Reax top Vortex Mixer weigh, and how big is it?
faqs.answer: The Reax top measures 134 x 105 x 172 mm and weighs 2.8 kg, a compact footprint that fits easily on a shared or space-limited bench.

faqs.question: Is the Reax top Vortex Mixer noisy?
faqs.answer: No. It runs under 50 dB(A) up to 2,500 rpm and under 58 dB(A) at its full 3,200 rpm, which is quiet for a mixer of this power.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Reax top Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: The part number of the Reax top Vortex Mixer is 541-10000-00. Inkarp is the authorized distributor for this Heidolph model in India.

products.overview: The Heidolph Reax control is the vortex mixer for work where the speed matters as much as the mixing. Electronic speed control and a graduated scale let you set a precise, repeatable rate from 0 to 2,500 rpm rather than guessing at a dial position. Its low range stays constant for shear-force-sensitive organisms, while the fixed 5 mm orbit delivers circular vibrating mixing on a compact, quiet bench footprint.

features.title: Electronic Speed Control
features.description: The speed is set electronically rather than by a mechanical dial position, which is what makes a defined rate possible. Applications that call for a specific speed get exactly that, run after run.

features.title: Graduated Speed Scale
features.description: The scaled display lets you read off and return to a setting. Once you have found the rate a particular sample needs, it is a number you can write into a method rather than a mark you have to re-find.

features.title: Range Starting at 0 rpm
features.description: The speed range begins at a standstill, so a sample can be brought up gradually instead of being hit with motion from the first second. For anything fragile, that first moment is where damage happens.

features.title: Constant Speed in the Low Range
features.description: Holding a genuinely low speed steady is harder than running fast, and it is exactly what shear-force-sensitive organisms need. The Reax control keeps the rate constant down at the gentle end of the range.

features.title: 5 mm Shaking Orbit
features.description: A fixed 5 mm orbit with circular vibrating movement does the mixing. The orbit stays the same; the speed you set decides how vigorously it works the sample.

features.title: Self-Resetting Overheat Protection

products.overview: The Heidolph Multi Reax is a multi-tube vortex mixer for high-throughput sample preparation. It mixes up to 26 tubes together, runs from 150 to 2,000 rpm with digital speed indication, uses a stable 3 mm circular vibrating orbit, and includes a timer up to 999 minutes with automatic stop and signal tone.

features.title: Up to 26 Tubes in One Run
features.description: The platform takes 12 tubes at 16 to 32 mm diameter, or 26 at 10 to 16 mm. Every tube in the rack sees the same speed for the same duration, which is what makes a batch comparable rather than a set of individually mixed samples.

features.title: Timer to 999 Minutes with Automatic Stop
features.description: Set the time and the Multi Reax stops the shaking itself when it expires, then sounds a tone. Long mixes no longer need watching, and a batch cannot accidentally run for twice as long because someone was pulled away.

features.title: Digital Speed Indication
features.description: Speed runs from 150 to 2,000 rpm and is shown digitally, so the setting is a figure you can record in a method and repeat exactly on the next batch.

features.title: Holds Falcon, Greiner and Snap-Lid Vessels
features.description: Falcon and Greiner tubes are both accommodated, and reaction vessels with snap-on lids are held securely too. In practice that covers most of what an analytical laboratory already has on the shelf.

features.title: 3 mm Shaking Orbit
features.description: A 3 mm orbit with circular vibrating movement drives the mixing. The tighter orbit is deliberate: a fully loaded rack needs a shorter, faster throw to stay stable, where a wider orbit would work against it.

features.title: 1.5 kg Load Limit
features.description: The platform is rated to 1.5 kg including tubes and contents. A full rack of larger tubes approaches this, so it is worth checking your loaded weight rather than assuming.

features.title: Quiet Under Load
features.description: Under 45 dB(A) in accordance with IEC 61010, which is quieter than the single-tube models and matters when a 999-minute batch is running beside people who are working.

features.title: Self-Resetting Overheat Protection
features.description: If the motor runs hot during a long batch, the overheat protection acts and then recovers on its own, so an extended run does not put the mixer out of service.

products.overview: The Heidolph Titramax 101 is a vibrating shaker for multi-well plates. It holds four plates on a 220 x 220 mm platform, uses a tight 3 mm circular vibrating orbit to move liquid inside small wells, runs from 150 to 1,350 rpm with continuously variable analogue control, and supports timed runs up to 120 minutes or continuous operation.

features.title: Four Multi-Well Plates
features.description: The 220 x 220 mm platform takes four multi-well plates at once, and every plate is shaken under the same conditions for the same time. That is what makes results across a batch comparable rather than a set of individually treated plates.

features.title: 3 mm Shaking Orbit
features.description: The orbit is deliberately short. Inside a microplate well there is very little room for liquid to travel, so a tight, fast throw does far more useful work than a wide, slow one. This is the specification that makes the model suitable for getting solids distributed and dissolved in the cavities.

features.title: Continuously Variable Speed, 150 to 1,350 rpm
features.description: Speed is adjusted steplessly on an analogue control, so you can settle on the exact intensity a plate and its contents need rather than jumping between preset steps.

features.title: Timer to 120 Minutes
features.description: Set a runtime for a defined process and the shaker handles it. For anything longer, or for protocols without a fixed endpoint, the shaker runs in continuous operation.

features.title: Continuous Operation
features.description: Beyond the timer, the Titramax 101 runs continuously, which suits extended incubation or dissolution steps where the shaking simply needs to keep going.

features.title: 2 kg Maximum Load
features.description: The platform is rated to 2 kg including plates and their contents. Four standard filled microplates sit comfortably within this, but it is worth checking if you shake deep-well plates or anything heavier.

features.title: Quiet Operation
features.description: Under 50 dB(A), so a long shaking run does not dominate a working bench.

features.title: Self-Resetting Overheat Protection
features.description: If the motor runs hot during an extended run, the overheat protection acts and then recovers on its own, so a long process does not put the shaker out of service.

features.title: Tolerant of Mains Fluctuation
features.description: The shaker accepts mains voltage fluctuation of ±10%, which is worth having where supply is not perfectly stable.

faqs.question: What is the Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker used for?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker is a plate shaker used for mixing in multi-well plates, and particularly for processes where solids have to be distributed or dissolved in the wells. It holds four multi-well plates and shakes them together under identical conditions.

faqs.question: How many plates does the Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker hold?

faqs.question: Why does the Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker have a 3 mm orbit?
faqs.answer: A microplate well gives liquid very little room to travel, so a short, fast orbit does far more useful work than a wide, slow one. The 3 mm orbit is what generates real movement inside the cavity, which is why this model suits distributing and dissolving solids in the wells.

faqs.question: Does the Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker have a timer?

faqs.question: Can the Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker run continuously?

faqs.question: How loud is the Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker?

sections.title: Speed, Orbit and Well Mixing
body: (Section swapped. Replaces "Performance and Utility Planning".)
Speed, orbit and well mixing on the Titramax 101 comes down to one question: is the liquid inside the well actually moving?

The 3 mm orbit is fixed, so speed is your variable. Too slow and the liquid rocks without turning over; enough speed and the short throw sets up genuine circulation in the cavity, which is what carries a solid into solution. Too fast with full wells and you risk liquid reaching the rim.

heroParagraphs: A wide, gentle orbit does very little inside a 6 mm well. The Heidolph Titramax 101 uses a short, fast 3 mm throw instead, which is what drives real movement in a cavity that small, and it is why this model suits work where solids have to be distributed or dissolved in the wells rather than merely swirled.

Four multi-well plates sit on the 220 x 220 mm platform, all shaken together under identical conditions. Speed is continuously variable from 150 to 1,350 rpm on an analogue control, so you can find the setting a plate needs and stay there.

The integrated timer runs to 120 minutes for defined processes, and the shaker runs in continuous operation when a protocol needs it. At under 50 dB(A) it stays quiet through a long run on a shared bench.

longForm.heroHook: Gentle motion keeps cells healthy. A 1.5 mm orbit keeps cultures suspended without exposing them to unnecessary shear.
longForm.heroLead: Not every laboratory sample benefits from aggressive mixing. Cell cultures, suspension cells, microorganisms, and delicate biological samples require continuous, uniform movement that distributes nutrients and oxygen while avoiding excessive mechanical stress. The Heidolph Titramax 100 Vibrating Shaker is designed specifically for these gentle mixing applications. Its precisely engineered 1.5 mm circular vibrating orbit keeps cultures evenly suspended without the vigorous agitation associated with larger orbit shakers. Continuously variable speeds from 150 to 1,350 rpm allow laboratories to match the shaking intensity to their specific protocol, whether maintaining mammalian cell cultures, mixing culture media, or supporting microbial growth. The spacious 220 × 220 mm platform accommodates multiple culture vessels while maintaining identical shaking conditions across every sample. A built-in 120-minute timer, continuous operation mode, quiet performance below 50 dB(A), and a compact footprint make the Titramax 100 an ideal solution for routine biological laboratories where reproducibility and sample integrity matter every day.

intro: The Titramax 100 Vibrating Shaker is a laboratory shaker with a 1.5 mm circular vibrating orbit, continuously variable speeds from 150 to 1,350 rpm, a 220 × 220 mm platform, and both timed and continuous operating modes for gentle biological sample mixing.

Gentle mixing is often the difference between maintaining healthy cultures and damaging sensitive samples. Cell cultures, microorganisms and suspension samples need continuous movement to prevent settling, distribute nutrients evenly and improve oxygen transfer, but excessive agitation can expose them to unnecessary shear stress.

heroParagraphs: Not every laboratory sample benefits from aggressive mixing. Cell cultures, suspension cells, microorganisms, and delicate biological samples require continuous, uniform movement that distributes nutrients and oxygen while avoiding excessive mechanical stress.

The Heidolph Titramax 100 Vibrating Shaker is designed specifically for these gentle mixing applications. Its precisely engineered 1.5 mm circular vibrating orbit keeps cultures evenly suspended without the vigorous agitation associated with larger orbit shakers. Continuously variable speeds from 150 to 1,350 rpm allow laboratories to match the shaking intensity to their specific protocol, whether maintaining mammalian cell cultures, mixing culture media, or supporting microbial growth.

The spacious 220 × 220 mm platform accommodates multiple culture vessels while maintaining identical shaking conditions across every sample. A built-in 120-minute timer, continuous operation mode, quiet performance below 50 dB(A), and a compact footprint make the Titramax 100 an ideal solution for routine biological laboratories where reproducibility and sample integrity matter every day.

faqs.question: What is the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Heidolph Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker is a laboratory platform shaker designed for gentle mixing of biological samples, cell cultures, and multi-well plates. It combines a 1.5 mm shaking orbit, 150–1,350 rpm speed range, and a platform that holds up to six microplates for high-throughput laboratory workflows.

faqs.question: What is the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker used for?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 is used for cell culture, biological assays, microbial cultivation, immunoassays, and high-throughput plate-based sample preparation. Its gentle orbital motion keeps samples uniformly suspended while minimizing shear stress, making it ideal for sensitive biological applications.

faqs.question: How many microplates can the Titramax 1000 hold?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 can hold up to six standard multi-well microplates on its 290 × 258 mm platform. This larger capacity enables laboratories to process more samples simultaneously while maintaining consistent shaking conditions across every plate.

faqs.question: What is the shaking orbit of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 uses a fixed 1.5 mm circular shaking orbit. This short orbit provides gentle, uniform agitation that distributes nutrients and maintains suspension without exposing sensitive biological samples to excessive mechanical stress.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 offers a continuously variable speed range of 150 to 1,350 rpm. Users can adjust the speed using the analogue control to match the requirements of different cell cultures, assays, and biological protocols.

faqs.question: Can the Titramax 1000 be used for temperature-controlled shaking?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 is designed to integrate with Heidolph's modular incubation system, allowing laboratories to perform temperature-controlled shaking for applications such as cell culture, microbial growth, and biological incubation.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 supports a maximum permissible load of 5 kg, including plates, vessels, and sample contents. The higher load capacity allows multiple fully loaded microplates to be processed in a single run.

faqs.question: Does the Titramax 1000 have a timer?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 includes an integrated timer adjustable up to 120 minutes. An acoustic signal indicates when the programmed shaking cycle has finished, and the shaker also supports continuous operation for longer experiments.

faqs.question: Can the Titramax 1000 operate continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 supports continuous operation, making it suitable for extended incubation, microbial cultivation, and long-duration biological experiments where uninterrupted shaking is required.

faqs.question: Is the Titramax 1000 suitable for cell culture applications?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 is specifically designed for cell culture applications. Its gentle 1.5 mm orbit keeps cells in suspension while reducing shear forces, helping maintain cell viability during long incubation periods.

faqs.question: What are the dimensions and weight of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 measures 320 × 128 × 375 mm and weighs 8 kg. Its larger platform accommodates six microplates while maintaining a compact footprint suitable for laboratory benches.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker?
faqs.answer: The official Heidolph part number for the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker is 544-12200-00.

faqs.question: What is the Rotamax 120 Orbital Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Heidolph Rotamax 120 Orbital Shaker is a laboratory shaker that uses a 20 mm orbital motion to produce uniform mixing in flasks, bottles, staining trays, and laboratory vessels. It offers continuously variable speeds from 20 to 300 rpm and supports loads up to 2 kg.

faqs.question: What is the Rotamax 120 Orbital Shaker used for?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 is used for solution preparation, culture media mixing, staining, destaining, sample extraction, washing procedures, and general laboratory mixing. Its orbital motion creates continuous liquid circulation for homogeneous sample preparation.

faqs.question: What is the shaking orbit of the Rotamax 120?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 has a fixed 20 mm orbital motion. This larger orbit moves the entire vessel in a circular path, creating effective liquid circulation and homogeneous mixing across a wide range of laboratory applications.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Rotamax 120?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 offers a continuously variable speed range of 20 to 300 rpm. Users can adjust the speed using the analogue control to suit different vessel sizes, sample volumes, and mixing requirements.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Rotamax 120?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 supports a maximum permissible load of 2 kg, including vessels and sample contents. This capacity makes it suitable for routine laboratory mixing using flasks, bottles, and staining trays.

faqs.question: Does the Rotamax 120 have a timer?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Rotamax 120 features an integrated timer adjustable up to 120 minutes for timed mixing protocols. It also supports continuous operation for longer laboratory workflows.

faqs.question: Can the Rotamax 120 operate continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Rotamax 120 supports continuous operation, making it suitable for extended mixing, extraction, staining, and washing applications that require uninterrupted agitation.

faqs.question: Which vessels are compatible with the Rotamax 120?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 is compatible with Erlenmeyer flasks, laboratory bottles, staining trays, culture vessels, and other laboratory containers when used with the appropriate platform accessories.

faqs.question: Is the Rotamax 120 suitable for cell culture?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 can be used for certain culture applications requiring orbital mixing. However, laboratories working with shear-sensitive cell cultures may prefer the Titramax series, which is specifically designed with gentle vibrating orbits for biological samples.

faqs.question: What are the dimensions and weight of the Rotamax 120?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 measures 245 × 125 × 310 mm and weighs 5.5 kg, providing a compact footprint suitable for routine laboratory use.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Rotamax 120 Orbital Shaker?
faqs.answer: The official Heidolph part number for the Rotamax 120 Orbital Shaker is 544-41200-00.

faqs.question: What is the Unimax 1010 Orbital Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Unimax 1010 Orbital Shaker is a laboratory orbital shaker designed for temperature-controlled shaking, automated workflows, cell culture, microbiology, pharmaceutical research, and routine sample preparation. It features a 10 mm orbital motion, 30–500 rpm speed range, 5 kg load capacity, and RS232 communication.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Unimax 1010 Orbital Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Unimax 1010 operates from 30 to 500 rpm, allowing gentle mixing for biological samples as well as faster orbital shaking for efficient liquid circulation.

faqs.question: What is the orbital motion of the Unimax 1010?
faqs.answer: The shaker uses a 10 mm orbital motion, providing uniform agitation and reproducible mixing across flasks, bottles, and other laboratory vessels.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Unimax 1010?

faqs.question: Does the Unimax 1010 automatically restart after a power failure?

faqs.question: Which applications is the Unimax 1010 best suited for?
faqs.answer: The Unimax 1010 is ideal for cell culture, microbial cultivation, pharmaceutical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, incubation workflows, and high-throughput laboratory mixing.

longForm.heroLead: The Heidolph Promax 1020 is built for laboratories that need controlled back-and-forth motion instead of orbital mixing. Its 32 mm reciprocating stroke produces strong linear agitation, making it ideal for separation, extraction, staining, washing, protein purification, and applications where directional movement delivers better results than circular motion. With a 30–250 rpm speed range, 5 kg load capacity, and compatibility with the Heidolph modular incubation system, the Promax 1020 supports both ambient and temperature-controlled workflows. The large 290 × 258 mm platform accommodates a wide range of vessels, while dedicated holders allow secure mounting of up to four 50–1000 mL separatory funnels for extraction applications. The programmable timer enables unattended operation, while the quiet EC motor delivers reliable performance throughout long laboratory processes.

longForm.heroHook: Powerful reciprocating motion for separation, extraction, and temperature-controlled shaking workflows.
heroParagraphs: The Heidolph Promax 1020 is built for laboratories that need controlled back-and-forth motion instead of orbital mixing. Its 32 mm reciprocating stroke produces strong linear agitation, making it ideal for separation, extraction, staining, washing, protein purification, and applications where directional movement delivers better results than circular motion.

With a 30–250 rpm speed range, 5 kg load capacity, and compatibility with the Heidolph modular incubation system, the Promax 1020 supports both ambient and temperature-controlled workflows. The large 290 × 258 mm platform accommodates a wide range of vessels, while dedicated holders allow secure mounting of up to four 50–1000 mL separatory funnels for extraction applications.
The programmable timer enables unattended operation, while the quiet EC motor delivers reliable performance throughout long laboratory processes.

faqs.question: What is the Vibramax 100 Orbital Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Heidolph Vibramax 100 is a compact circular vibrating shaker designed for suspension, solubility studies, leaching studies, and routine laboratory mixing applications.

faqs.question: What is the Vibramax 100 Orbital Shaker used for?
faqs.answer: It is used for particle suspension, reagent mixing, sample preparation, solubility testing, leaching studies, and other laboratory workflows requiring vigorous mixing.

faqs.question: What speed range does the Vibramax 100 provide?
faqs.answer: The shaker offers continuously adjustable speeds from 150 to 2,500 rpm, allowing users to optimize mixing intensity for different applications.

faqs.question: Which laboratory applications require a circular vibrating shaker instead of an orbital shaker?
faqs.answer: Circular vibrating shakers are preferred for suspension, solubility, and leaching studies where rapid, high-frequency agitation improves sample dispersion and mixing.

faqs.question: What speed should I use for suspension and solubility studies?
faqs.answer: Lower speeds are suitable for gentle mixing, while higher speeds provide vigorous agitation for dissolving solids and keeping particles uniformly suspended.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Vibramax 100?
faqs.answer: The Vibramax 100 supports a maximum permissible load of 2 kg, including the platform, vessels, and sample contents.

faqs.question: What platform size does the Vibramax 100 have?
faqs.answer: It features a 220 × 220 mm usable platform that accommodates a wide range of laboratory vessels and optional accessories.

faqs.question: Can the Vibramax 100 hold different container sizes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Optional tension roller attachments securely hold bottles, flasks, and containers of different sizes during high-speed shaking.

faqs.question: Does the Vibramax 100 include a timer?
faqs.answer: Yes. It includes a 120-minute timer with an acoustic signal at the end of the run and also supports continuous operation.

faqs.question: Is the Vibramax 100 suitable for continuous operation?
faqs.answer: Yes. The shaker is designed for both timed and continuous operation, making it suitable for routine as well as extended laboratory processes.

faqs.question: Is the Vibramax 100 noisy?
faqs.answer: No. It operates at less than 50 dB(A), providing quiet operation even during extended shaking cycles.

faqs.question: Does the Vibramax 100 include overheat protection?
faqs.answer: Yes. The shaker features self-resetting overheat protection, helping protect the motor during prolonged operation.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Vibramax 100?
faqs.answer: The official Heidolph Vibramax 100 part number is 544-21200-00.

longForm.heroLead: The Heidolph Vibramax 100 is designed for laboratory workflows where vigorous circular vibration delivers better sample suspension than gentle orbital motion. Its 3 mm orbit combined with speeds from 150 to 2,500 rpm creates rapid, uniform agitation for suspending solids, dissolving compounds, and performing leaching studies. A 220 × 220 mm platform accommodates a wide range of laboratory vessels, while the optional tension roller attachment securely holds different container sizes. Together with the non-slip rubber mat, samples remain stable even during high-speed operation. The integrated 120-minute timer supports repeatable protocols, while continuous operation handles longer experiments. With a compact footprint, quiet operation, and reliable performance, the Vibramax 100 fits naturally into research, analytical, environmental, pharmaceutical, and academic laboratories.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert Orbital Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert is a premium orbital shaker with a 20 mm orbit, 1–530 rpm speed range, programmable profiles, and automation-ready connectivity for advanced laboratory workflows. It is designed for laboratories requiring high reproducibility and digital workflow management.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert used for?
faqs.answer: It is used for cell culture, media preparation, sample extraction, pharmaceutical research, molecular biology, and routine laboratory mixing. The shaker delivers uniform agitation for both research and quality control applications.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert?
faqs.answer: The shaker operates from 1 to 530 rpm, allowing precise control for gentle mixing as well as vigorous sample agitation. This wide range supports diverse laboratory applications.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert?
faqs.answer: The Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert supports up to 15 kg, making it suitable for multiple flasks, bottles, microplates, and heavy laboratory vessels. This enables high-throughput sample processing.

faqs.question: What is the shaking orbit of the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert?
faqs.answer: The shaker features a 20 mm orbital motion that provides efficient and homogeneous mixing across different vessel sizes. This ensures consistent sample agitation throughout the platform.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert save shaking methods?
faqs.answer: Yes. It allows users to save profiles and favourite methods, enabling routine experiments to be repeated with identical parameters. This improves reproducibility and reduces setup time.

faqs.question: Is the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert suitable for laboratory automation?
faqs.answer: Yes. Its programmable platform positioning, USB interfaces, and RS232 communication make it ideal for robotic sample handling and automated laboratory workflows. It integrates easily into modern digital laboratories.

faqs.question: How does programmable platform alignment improve automated workflows?
faqs.answer: Programmable platform alignment positions the platform with up to 2° precision, allowing robots and automated systems to load and unload samples accurately. This reduces positioning errors and improves automation reliability.

faqs.question: What laboratory applications benefit from programmable method storage?
faqs.answer: Method storage is valuable for validated pharmaceutical methods, routine QC testing, cell culture protocols, and repetitive research workflows, where identical shaking conditions must be reproduced every time.

faqs.question: What timer functions does the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert provide?
faqs.answer: The digital timer can be set from 1 second to 999 hours 59 minutes 59 seconds, making it suitable for both short laboratory procedures and long-duration experiments. Continuous operation is also supported.

faqs.question: What communication interfaces are available on the Hei-SHAKE Orbital Expert?
faqs.answer: The shaker includes USB A, USB B, and RS232 interfaces for data logging, remote control, software integration, and automation. These interfaces simplify digital laboratory workflows.

faqs.question: Is the touchscreen compatible with laboratory gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The capacitive touchscreen is designed to remain responsive while wearing laboratory gloves, ensuring convenient operation in routine laboratory environments.

Ready to install. The unit ships with the flat rubber mat 1000 and an upgrade set including the flat rubber mat 2000.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-SHAKE Wave Core 3D Shaker used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-SHAKE Wave Core 3D Shaker is used for gentle sample movement, continuous rinsing, biological sample handling, and laboratory workflows requiring controlled three-dimensional motion.

faqs.question: How does the 3D wave movement of the Hei-SHAKE Wave Core support laboratory workflows?
faqs.answer: The 3D wave movement creates gentle multi-directional sample motion, making it suitable for applications where uniform contact, continuous rinsing, and low-stress sample handling are required.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Hei-SHAKE Wave Core 3D Shaker?
faqs.answer: The shaker provides a speed range of 1 to 80 rpm, allowing controlled movement for sensitive biological and research applications.

faqs.question: Why does the Hei-SHAKE Wave Core 3D Shaker have a 5° tilt angle?
faqs.answer: The 5° tilt angle helps reduce foaming and minimizes risks such as glass breakage and liquid spill-over during gentle shaking applications.

faqs.question: How does the Hei-SHAKE Wave Core support continuous rinsing applications?
faqs.answer: The 3D wave motion provides continuous sample movement, ensuring consistent liquid contact and supporting workflows that require controlled rinsing conditions.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-SHAKE Wave Core 3D Shaker be integrated into automated laboratory workflows?
faqs.answer: Yes. The RS232 interface enables connection with external systems, PC-based control, and semi-automated laboratory process integration.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Hei-SHAKE Wave Core 3D Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Hei-SHAKE Wave Core 3D Shaker supports a maximum permissible load of 15 kg, allowing multiple sample vessels to be handled during operation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a 3D shaker and an orbital shaker?
faqs.answer: A 3D shaker creates wave-like multi-directional movement, while an orbital shaker produces circular movement. The Hei-SHAKE Wave Core is designed for gentle sample handling and continuous rinsing workflows.

faqs.question: What applications require a low-speed 3D shaker?
faqs.answer: Low-speed 3D shakers are commonly used for biological samples, rinsing procedures, incubation support, and workflows where excessive agitation may affect sample integrity.

intro: The overview of the Duomax 1030 Rocking Shaker covers its role in laboratories requiring gentle movement, controlled sample handling, and compact bench-top operation.

The Heidolph Duomax 1030 Rocking Shaker provides a controlled rocking movement designed for applications requiring gentle and consistent sample motion. The 5° tilt angle supports low-amplitude rocking, helping maintain smooth liquid movement while reducing unnecessary agitation.
The anti-slip rubber mat keeps containers securely positioned during operation, while the adjustable speed range allows users to select suitable rocking conditions based on sample requirements.
